content.value_statement: Real-time voice apps need streaming audio, authentication, session state, and event handling. This skill gives Python patterns for Azure AI Voice Live clients.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation for azure-ai-voicelive, aiohttp, and azure-identity.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential and API key connection setup.
Explains session settings for modalities, voices, audio formats, tools, and turn detection.
Shows base64 PCM16 input and response audio handling.
Lists VoiceLiveConnection resources and common event types.
Provides patterns for manual turns, interruptions, conversation items, and error handling.
limitations: Requires an Azure Cognitive Services endpoint and valid credentials.
Does not provide a complete production app or microphone implementation.
Examples need testing against your installed SDK version and Azure resource configuration.
Function tools and audio playback require application-specific implementation.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Voice Assistant
use_cases.description: Use the connection, session, and event examples to build a first Azure Voice Live assistant.

use_cases.title: Plan Streaming Audio Flows
use_cases.description: Map microphone input, base64 audio buffers, response audio, and interruption handling before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Azure Voice Integration
use_cases.description: Check authentication choices, turn detection, voice options, and error handling for an existing design.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up an Azure AI Voice Live Python project. Include packages, environment variables, and a simple connection flow.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Voice Live session for a customer support assistant. Include voice choice, audio formats, turn detection, and concise instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Streaming Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Voice Live event handling plan. Suggest how to process transcripts, audio responses, interruptions, errors, and completion.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Function Calling
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for a Voice Live assistant that calls functions during conversation. Include data flow, errors, and testing steps.

output_examples.input: I need a first Voice Live setup plan.
output: Install the Azure Voice Live and identity packages.
Choose DefaultAzureCredential unless API key access is required.
Set the Azure endpoint in the environment.
Open a connection and update the session settings.
Run one event loop test to confirm responses arrive.

output_examples.input: I need to stream microphone audio and play responses.
output: Capture mono PCM16 audio in chunks.
Encode each chunk before appending it to the input buffer.
Commit the buffer when the user turn ends.
Decode response audio chunks before playback.
Cancel and clear output when the user interrupts.

output_examples.input: I need a production readiness review.
output: Validate audio formats against the selected channel.
Handle connection closed, API errors, and response completion.
Limit transcript logging to approved data.
Test latency, interruption, and reconnect behavior.

best_practices: Validate sample rate, channel count, and audio format before streaming.
Handle response completion, errors, closed connections, and user interruptions explicitly.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode Azure API keys or endpoints in source files.
Do not assume microphone, playback, and network behavior work without device tests.
Do not ignore event ordering, cancellation, or buffer cleanup.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build Python clients for Azure AI Voice Live real-time voice sessions.

faq.question: Does it include a complete app?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused patterns for connection setup, session configuration, events, audio, and errors.

faq.question: Which authentication method is recommended?
faq.answer: DefaultAzureCredential is preferred for production. API keys are shown for simple cases that require them.

faq.question: Can it handle microphone audio?
faq.answer: It shows the expected audio buffer flow, but microphone capture must be implemented in your app.

faq.question: Does it explain function calling?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows the event path for function call arguments and returning function outputs.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
